newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo, drug stocks up after ADR gains.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo, drug stocks up after ADR gains.

text.p: Shares in Glaxo Wellcome Plc led drug stocks higher in early trade on Tuesday, up two percent after strength in its ADRs in the U.S., dealers said.
Glaxo shares were up 26-1/2p at 13.27-1/2 stg by 0724 GMT after its ADRs rose $5/8 to $43-1/4 and SmithKline Beecham Plc rose 15p to 11.82-1/2 stg after its ADRs climbed $1-5/8 to $95-3/4

An agreement between makers of a generic version of Zantac could also be positive for Glaxo since only one company will sell a version in the U.S. until the end of the year, meaning less pressure on profit margins for that time, dealers said.
Separately, Zeneca Group Plc shrugged off weakness in its ADRs, to be up 22-1/2p at 20.25 stg after naming Jonathan Symons, chairman of KPMG's global pharmaceutical group as its new finance director.

Zeneca said Symons' knowledge of the drug industry would enable him to make an immediate contribution to its business. The company's first-half results on August 7 are expected to show a rise in pre-tax profits to between 623 million stg and 670 million from 610 million a year before.
